subject: Recap: TTFT targets & hybrid SSE/WebSocket chunk cadence — next actions
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris@vartix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: TTFT targets & hybrid SSE/WebSocket chunk cadence — next actions

Hi Chris —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and we’ll adjust.

Summary of what we discussed (performance & streaming):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): target baseline of ~60ms median; goal p95 < 150ms for streaming start-of-response for typical user prompts.
- Throughput: initial pilot sizing = 500 RPS sustained (steady-state), peak bursts up to ~1,200 RPS for short windows.
- Concurrency: expected concurrent sessions ~200 active websocket/SSE connections during peak.
- Streaming mode: hybrid approach — prefer SSE for browser/web clients; WebSocket for mobile apps where connection half-duplex and lower tail latency is required.
- Chunk cadence: target chunk emit cadence of ~150–250ms for interactive flows. Aim for 1–3 tokens per chunk to reduce tail amplification; allow dynamic bursting for longer outputs.
- Fallbacks: fallback to smaller model variant when queueing/latency breaches SLO; automated routing policy and graceful truncation options.

Telemetry / SLOs we’ll capture in pilot:
- TTFT median and p95 (end-to-end, measured at client SDK)
- Token-per-chunk distribution and inter-chunk gaps
- Request queue latency and model execution time
- Error rate / aborted streams

Attachments I’m sending with this message: redwood-ttft-proposal.pdf (pilot scope & pricing), vartix-ttft-loadshape.csv (template for your load shapes), telemetry-spec.xlsx (fields we’ll need).

Immediate next steps (agreed on call):
1) Vartix to share realistic 48-hour load shape (CSV) — Chris / engineering — by EOD Thursday 9/16.
2) Redwood: prepare pilot config + baseline SLOs and a recommended chunk cadence matrix (we’ll provide an initial config within 2 business days).
3) Schedule technical kickoff (30–45m) with Vartix SRE + Redwood infra (Ben) next week; propose Wed 9/22 10:00 PT.
4) Contract touchpoint: Vartix legal will share procurement checklist / contract cadence — add contracts@vartix.ai into thread.

Open question from our side: for long-running generation flows (~>30s), do you need steady interim tokens every 200ms or can the client tolerate irregular bursts? Please call this out in the load shape.

Thanks — I’ll queue Ben to draft the pilot config once we have the load CSV.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
<aisha@redwood.com>

--

- redwood-ttft-proposal.pdf (proposal, 6 pages)

From: Chris Nolan <chris@vartix.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, contracts@vartix.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: TTFT targets & hybrid SSE/WebSocket chunk cadence — next actions

Aisha —

Thanks for the thorough recap, this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from the engineering side:
- Mobile team prefers WebSocket when available; main concern is p99 tail for TTFT on cellular. Mobile can accept slightly larger first chunk (up to 5 tokens) to reduce number of round trips.
- For browser clients, SSE is preferred to keep things simple. We will likely use a mix depending on platform.
- Load shape: we’ll send a 48-hour sample tomorrow; it will include per-endpoint mixes and a few synthetic spike scenarios.
- Contract: we’ll loop in procurement but likely need a 30-day pilot T&Cs and a cap on spend during pilot.

Question: Can Redwood provide an SDK-side heartbeat/priming option to reduce cold TTFT (e.g., warm connections or a tiny priming token)? If so, can Ben include a note in the pilot config about recommended priming size?

Appreciate it — will send the CSV by 9/16 EOD.

—Chris
Head of Engineering, Vartix
chris@vartix.ai

Subject: Re: Recap: TTFT targets & hybrid SSE/WebSocket chunk cadence — next actions

Chris —

Great — yes, we have two levers for reducing cold-start TTFT:
1) SDK priming: small priming request (≈ 8–16 tokens) that pre-warms KV cache + model context — typically reduces TTFT by ~30–50ms in our tests. We’ll provide a default priming size and an opt-out flag.
2) Persistent warm connections + occasional keepalive traffic (heartbeat) — easy to enable from client side; we’ll document recommended keepalive interval for mobile and web.

Ben — can you include priming config + expected delta in the pilot config? Also, please include a short note on how our routing/fallback will behave if the model variant trips the latency threshold.

Chris — once we have your CSV we’ll:
- Share a pilot config (JSON) with chunk cadence matrix and priming defaults.
- Stand up a small test run in Redwood's dedicated pilot cluster and share telemetry dashboards.

Proposed kickoff: Wed 9/22 10:00 PT — does that still work for you? If not, offer two alternate windows.

Thanks,
Aisha
